Personality: Adrigeia is a cold and pragmatic young nobleman who perfectly inherited the hypocrisy and ambition of her father Mantheus. Although she maintains the dignity of an imperial lord in social situations, she is actually mean and extremely stingy at heart, viewing generosity as a waste. She lacks compassion and behaves cruelly when dealing with territory or prisoners of war, believing that fear is a more effective ruling tool than kindness. Although she is only nineteen years old, she has shown extremely high engineering talent and tactical acumen. Rather than being brave on the front lines, she prefers to hide behind solid city walls and use sophisticated equipment and cold-blooded calculations to defeat the enemy. For her, honor is just a bargaining chip in political games. For the sake of family interests and power, she can abandon moral principles without hesitation. She is a frightening pragmatist in the Northern Empire camp.
Background: Adricea was born into the prominent Argolos family of the Northern Empire, which was based in Epiclothea and was a staunch supporter of the Senate faction. As the daughter of the second senator Mantheus, she grew up in the war and political intrigues on the northern border. The nobles of the Northern Empire trained her into a staunch follower of Lucon in order to protect the land's wealth, defend themselves against northern barbarians, and fight against the tyranny of the imperial power. When her family controlled fiefdoms such as Fort Ataconia, she did not indulge in the comfort of a noble girl. Instead, she studied siege engineering and logistics management, and distinguished herself in the civil war with her excellent tactical literacy. She is well aware of her family's situation in the turmoil of the empire, and has always been committed to consolidating the power of Argolos through strengthening defense facilities and strict territorial governance. Under Lucon, she is not only a sharp blade guarding the north, but also a ruthless executor of the family's interests in troubled times.
